summary: Colville NF lookout on Snyder Hill: a 10-ft pole L-4 tower from about 1937, destroyed or removed in 1958; footings, stovepipe and anchors remain on the ridge.

facts.design: 10-ft pole tower with an L-4 cab; platform patrol tower half a mile west on the west ridge
facts.status_note: Destroyed in 1958 (firelookout.com, Willhite Web) or removed (Former Fire Lookout Sites). Willhite Web's recent photos show four footings, part of a stove, a stovepipe and many anchors on the east ridge.

access.note: Snyder Hill Road (FR 050) has two gates with seasonal closures; Willhite Web advises July to August 14, when both gates are open. The site is on Colville National Forest land.

visit.trail_note: Cross the Ione Bridge, take Sullivan Lake Road 1.4 miles to FR 050, drive 8.7 miles of gravel to a ridge junction, then walk the final mile, which is overgrowing in places (Willhite Web).

events.note: Around 1937: 10-ft pole tower with an L-4 cab on the east ridge near the summit, plus a platform patrol tower half a mile west (Former Fire Lookout Sites, firelookout.com, Willhite Web)
Aerial pictures from 1955 still show the cab (Willhite Web)
Lookout came down in 1958. firelookout.com and Willhite Web say destroyed; Former Fire Lookout Sites says removed; Rex's page marks it Removed.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Former Fire Lookout Sites says the lookout was removed in 1958; firelookout.com and Willhite Web say it was destroyed that year. All agree on 1958. The story reports both words.

Former Fire Lookout Sites and firelookout.com give the site as 5,426 ft (1,654 m); Willhite Web gives 5,437 feet, which may be a summit figure. The brief's 1,653.8 m matches the 5,426 ft figure, so it is kept.

notes_for_editor: Dates agree across all sources (about 1937, destroyed or removed 1958). Only the removal wording differs. Present-day remains come from Willhite Web's photo captions (2026 for the stovepipe); the patrol tower site and phone line are mentioned but not in the story's remains list. Access is restricted by seasonal gates on FR 050, not closed. The summit has a USGS benchmark placed in 1992 and sits in Maitlen Creek RNA; neither is in the story. Height_m 3.0 reads the 10-ft pole as tower height.
